evidence.why: Shows basis selection, facing guard, denominator switch and setter call.

facts.rationale: Replaces an unqualified actual-motion freeze/synchronization description with the exact selected-basis behavior.
facts.value: Computes and requests a tier-specific walking animation rate from a selected movement basis: cached walk.x0 when ground-friction multiplier is below one, otherwise gr_vel. A non-forward selected basis requests zero; a forward basis is divided by the active tier's stored rate denominator.

evidence.why: Physics writes scaled target into cached basis.

facts.rationale: Preserves proven walking association without claiming exact synchronization to actual movement.
facts.value: Supplies common rate control for ordinary Walk, CargoWalk and Donkey HeavyWalk animations. Its animation-speed basis can be a cached scaled target rather than actual ground velocity, and the animation setter can defer applying the requested rate.

evidence.why: Complete rate calculation and missing default.

facts.rationale: Adds source-visible invariants and the external setter's optional branch.
facts.value: Uses walk.x0 only for a ground-friction multiplier strictly below one, otherwise gr_vel. If basis*facing_dir <= 0 it requests rate zero; otherwise it requests ABS(basis) divided by the matching Slow/Middle/Fast denominator. The switch lacks a default and can leave anim_rate uninitialized for an invalid offset; denominators and exceptional floats are unchecked. ftAnim_SetAnimRate caches the request instead of immediately applying it when x2223_b0 is set. No motion transition is performed.

evidence.why: Equality guard, phase arithmetic and callback invocation.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes requested callback entry from direct state mutation and exact phase preservation.
facts.value: Detects a change in the desired base-plus-walk-tier motion and synchronously delegates action-specific entry through a callback, supplying an integer-quantized destination frame calculated from the current animation cycle phase.

facts.rationale: Active callers establish gameplay use while integer truncation limits the guarantee.
facts.value: Supports transitions among walking animation tiers without always restarting at frame zero: for valid animation spans it maps the current cycle phase into a destination-tier span, truncates to an integer frame, then calls the ordinary Walk, CargoWalk or HeavyWalk entry adapter. This is approximate phase continuity, not a guarantee of visually seamless or exact phase preservation.

evidence.why: End frame comes from normal or blend skeleton.

facts.rationale: Makes quantization, callback lifetime, equality boundary and invalid-input preconditions explicit.
facts.value: If desired base+tier equals motion_id, returns without calling the callback. Otherwise selects destination span D, obtains end frame E, computes q=(s32)(cur_anim_frame/E), then destination=(s32)(D*((cur_anim_frame-E*q)/E)), and calls arg_cb once with the same object and destination converted to float. The callback is not retained and is not null-checked. Nonfinite/zero E and unrepresentable integer conversions are unguarded. The switch default reports an error and invokes HSD_ASSERT(71,0), but valid classifier outputs select one of its three cases.

evidence.why: Entry, animation, tier update and physics flow.
Prepared floor-tangent vectors, not position integration.

facts.rationale: Replaces the TU's unconditional phase-preservation and actual-motion playback claims.
facts.value: Entry classifies absolute gr_vel and chooses a caller-supplied base plus Slow/Middle/Fast offset. Tier updates delegate only when the desired motion differs, with integer-quantized phase mapping. Animation processing requests zero for a non-forward selected basis or a tier-scaled rate otherwise; the basis is cached walk.x0 below unit ground-friction multiplier and gr_vel otherwise, and the setter may defer application. Physics refreshes walk.x0 from scaled target velocity, prepares friction-aware acceleration and floor-aligned movement vectors. Valid objects, initialized walk metadata and usable animation spans are required; the TU does not validate them.
